newsitem.title: USA: White House pleased at EU deal on Boeing.
newsitem.headline: White House pleased at EU deal on Boeing.

text.p: The White House expressed pleasure that the European Union reached agreement Wednesday with Boeing on its $15 billion deal to merge with McDonnell Douglas.

"We're very pleased that the EU has recognised that Boeing went the extra mile in proposing a compromise solution and we hope that the commissioners will approve this formally when they meet next week," an administration official said.

The official said the White House was in contact with Boeing "throughout the process," but declined to say whether administration officials had leaned on Boeing to make concessions demanded by the EU.
"It's a complex question," the official said. "We were not holding a gun to their head. No one forced Boeing to do this."

Boeing agreed to license patents obtained under military contracts to the European consortium, Airbus Industrie; to keep McDonnell Douglas commercial aircraft as a separate legal entity for 10 years; and to drop enforcement of existing exclusive-provider agreements with airlines and not to agree to new ones until 2007.
